description: Na₂O crystallizes in the hexagonal P̅62m space group. There are two inequivalent Na¹⁺ sites. In the first Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to five O²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaO₅ square pyramids that share corners with ten equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids, corners with six equivalent NaO₄ tetrahedra, edges with six equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids, and edges with six equivalent NaO₄ tetrahedra. There is one shorter (2.51 Å) and four longer (2.55 Å) Na-O bond lengths. In the second Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to four O²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with six equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids, corners with ten equivalent NaO₄ tetrahedra, edges with six equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids, and edges with two equivalent NaO₄ tetrahedra. There are two shorter (2.28 Å) and two longer (2.38 Å) Na-O bond lengths. There are two inequivalent O²⁻ sites. In the first O²⁻ site, O²⁻ is bonded in a 9-coordinate geometry to nine Na¹⁺ atoms. In the second O²⁻ site, O²⁻ is bonded in a 9-coordinate geometry to nine Na¹⁺ atoms.
